projects.name: PubTator3 / BioREx (+LinkBERT) — NCBI
projects.status: active (weekly updates; API answered 2026-10-23; BioREx repo pushed 2025-05; bulk files dated 2026-10-06 already on Dan's disk)
projects.what_it_does: NCBI's PubMed-scale NER+normalization+relation extraction. Entities normalized to NCBI Gene, MeSH (chem/disease), dbSNP/HGVS, NCBI Taxonomy, Cellosaurus. Relations via BioREx (document-level, multi-sentence) with PubMedBERT swapped for LinkBERT: BioRED test F1 74.4 -> 79.6 (BioREx) -> 82.0 (LinkBERT). 12 relation types over 8 entity-pair types (Associate, Positive_Correlate, Negative_Correlate, Compare, Cotreat, Interact, Drug_Interact, Cause, Inhibit, Treat, Stimulate, Prevent). ~36M abstracts + 6M PMC full texts. projects.relevance_to_biolean: This is the free, maintained baseline edge set for all 28.5M abstracts; no LLM pass can match its cost (zero) or its strict-schema F1 (0.82 vs <=0.31 for prompted frontier LLMs). Use it as the backbone graph and spend LLM budget only on what it lacks: hedging/negation, novelty-vs-background, nested statements, RO/GO-typed predicates, and the canonical-paper statements. Limits: mostly correlation-style predicates (direction only for Cause/Inhibit/Treat/Stimulate/Prevent), no negation, speculation or novelty flags in bulk output, ~74% of its errors are cross-sentence.

projects.name: BioRED benchmark family (BioRED corpus, BioCreative VIII track, directionality + novelty extension)
projects.status: active (directionality extension Jan 2025; track overview published Database 2024; JTIS follow-up 2025)
projects.what_it_does: Document-level gold standard for gene/disease/chemical/variant relations with a novelty flag (new finding vs cited background). BioCreative VIII (14 teams, 94 runs) best F1: with gold entities 77.2 pair / 59.0 type / 59.2 novelty / 44.6 all-correct; end-to-end from raw text 55.8 / 43.0 / 42.7 / 32.8. Lai et al. 2025 add subject/object direction (10,864 annotations, IAA 89.96%); their multi-task model gets 37.0 F1 on relation+direction+novelty and 42.7 on relation+novelty vs fine-tuned GPT-3.5 38.5 and fine-tuned Llama-3.2-11B 37.5; zero-shot GPT-4 42.9 on entity pairs only. Association/Bind are inherently undirected, chem-chem Cotreatment has 55 training pairs.
projects.relevance_to_biolean: These numbers set realistic expectations: entity-pair detection is ~0.8 F1, but the three things BioLean actually needs for proofs (relation type, direction of effect, is-this-new-evidence) are each ~0.4-0.6, and jointly ~0.35-0.45, for the best systems in 2025. Novelty is the closest existing label to 'how established' vs 'background restated' and is the right place to start an evidence-weight schema. The corpus is also the obvious dev/eval set for any BioLean extractor.

projects.name: Critic-based verification for LLM biomedical RE (Assi, Karabadji, Elati, Dhifli)
projects.status: paper only (PromptEng 2026 workshop at WebConf, Dubai, June 2026); no released code found
projects.what_it_does: Measures frontier and local LLMs on 75 BioRED test abstracts, then adds a second 'critic' prompt that re-reads each extracted (s,p,o) against the text and labels it CORRECT / NEGATED / SPECULATIVE / INCORRECT. Few-shot + critic: Gemini 3 Pro P 0.383 R 0.257 F1 0.307 (best); Claude 4.5 Sonnet P 0.331 -> 0.741 after critic (92.6% false-positive reduction) but recall ~0.07; extended thinking lifts single-pass precision 33.1 -> 55.7%; Llama-3.2 local F1 0.114, ~10 s/doc. Zero-shot without critic: F1 0.064 with 1,089 false positives. All far below supervised (they cite 62.8; PubTator3's own model is 82.0).
projects.relevance_to_biolean: The most honest 2026 datapoint on what prompting alone buys you on a strict schema: precision can be bought (critic), recall cannot. For BioLean this argues for LLMs as high-precision annotators over a recall-oriented backbone (PubTator3), and for the critic's NEGATED/SPECULATIVE labels as a cheap, ready-made epistemic field for each statement. Note the 'precision floor' was schema misalignment, not reasoning: a tight Biolink/RO predicate list plus examples mattered more than model size.
projects.reusable_assets: Prompt designs (extraction + critic) printed in the paper; none otherwise.
key_refs: Reasoning vs. Critic-Based Verification for Biomedical Relation Extraction with Large Language Models, CEUR-WS Vol-4258 paper 1, PromptEng 2026

projects.name: OntoGPT / SPIRES (Monarch Initiative)
projects.status: active (v1.2.0 released 2026-09-09; LiteLLM multi-provider; 'term validation after extraction' added; 69 open issues)
projects.what_it_does: Schema-driven zero-shot extraction: you write a LinkML schema with nested classes and ontology-valued slots; SPIRES recursively prompts the LLM to fill it, then grounds every value by ontology lookup (OAK) rather than trusting LLM-emitted IDs. Published eval (Database 2024): BC5CDR chemical-induces-disease F1 41.2 (GPT-3.5, chunked) / 43.8 (no chunking, stronger model) vs 57 for the best supervised 2015 system and 45.0 for BioGPT; grounding 97-98/100 correct GO and MONDO IDs via SPIRES vs 1-3/100 when the LLM emits IDs itself (GPT-4-turbo got 18/100 on MONDO and sometimes refused). Authors warn OpenAI-scale corpora may be prohibitively expensive.
projects.relevance_to_biolean: Closest existing tool to Dan's 'DNApol (GO function) copies (GO process) DNA (SO term)' idea: the schema can require subject/predicate/object slots whose ranges are GO/RO/SO/CHEBI, and grounding is done against the OBO terms Dan already has locally (6M terms). Nested schemas also fit 'mechanism' statements (drug -> target -> process -> phenotype) better than flat triples. Weakness: mid-pack relation F1, no evidence/hedging model, and it is a per-document tool, not a PubMed-scale pipeline.
projects.reusable_assets: ontogpt on PyPI (1.2.0), LinkML templates (incl. biological process, drug mechanism, chemical-to-disease), OAK grounding adapters; templates are plain YAML you can fork for a BioLean statement schema.

projects.name: Gilda + LLM disambiguation (grounding stack: Gilda, scispaCy, BERN2, Ye & Mitchell 2025)
projects.status: Gilda active (1.6.1 on PyPI 2026-06-11, repo pushed 2026-06-29; web service answered a live POST today: semaglutide -> CHEBI:167574). scispaCy maintained (0.6.2, 2025-10). BERN2 dormant (repo last push 2024-03-28; demo site still serving).
projects.what_it_does: Gilda: lexical + ~1,000 learned disambiguation models over ~2M names from HGNC, UniProt, FamPlex, CHEBI, GO, DOID, EFO, HP, MeSH, Adeft; the grounder behind INDRA. Ye & Mitchell (ACL 2025 short) show that putting an LLM as the disambiguator after an alias-matching candidate generator gives a new SOTA on several biomedical EL sets, up to +16 accuracy points, no fine-tuning. Older head-to-head on BC5CDR (2023): BERN2 0.939/0.966 (disease/chem) vs GPT-4 retrieve-rank 0.901/0.947 vs scispaCy 0.853 chem. RELATE (2025) applies the same idea to predicates: SapBERT retrieval over Biolink predicates + LLM rerank, ChemProt 52% exact / 94% acc@10, explicit negation handling (found 77 negated assertions in 2,400 HEAL abstracts; 'fails to affect' type implicit negation is the hard residue).
projects.relevance_to_biolean: Settles the grounding design: never let the LLM invent identifiers; build a lexical index over the local OBO dump (Gilda-style, or Gilda itself, which already covers CHEBI/GO/HP/DOID/MeSH and ties into Dan's INDRA cache), then let an LLM pick among candidates. Do the same for predicates against RO/Biolink. Gilda's grounding.indra.bio is usable now; running Gilda locally on 112 cores is trivial. BERN2 should not be a dependency.

projects.name: iKraph (Insilicom / FSU; LitCoin NLP Challenge winner)
projects.status: maintained (Nature Machine Intelligence 2025; repo last push 2025-04; Zenodo dump Feb 2025; data cutoff May 2023)
projects.what_it_does: PubMed-wide KG built with the pipeline that won LitCoin 2022 (RoBERTa-large/PubMedBERT ensembles, Ab3P, document-level RE; not LLM-based): 34M abstracts -> 10.7M entities, 30.8M relations, plus 40 databases and RNA-seq-derived edges; 12 entity types, 53 relation types. LitCoin scores: NER Jaccard 0.918, RE 0.633. A direction classifier (F1 0.924 CV; trained on 4,572 hand-labelled relations: 2,009 forward, 1,611 reverse, 952 undirected) turns correlations into a directed 'causal KG'. Novelty is a pipeline stage. Evidence aggregation by 'probabilistic semantic reasoning': P = 1 - prod(1 - p_mention) across abstracts; indirect paths scored by multiplying link probabilities; only the top relation type per pair kept. Journal/citation/date weighting is explicitly future work. Validated on COVID-19 repurposing (1,200 candidates; ~1/3 of early ones later supported).
projects.relevance_to_biolean: The nearest thing to Dan's 'weighted edges + inference over paths' that exists at PubMed scale, and it is downloadable. Its noisy-OR aggregation is a defensible first evidence score for a biolib lemma; its path-product rule is a (weak) prototype of 'proof weight'. Gaps BioLean can fill: contradiction is resolved by keeping one type per pair, no hedging, no source quality, no formal semantics. Species handling: entities are NCBI Gene IDs, so cross-species merging is on you.
projects.reusable_assets: Full KG on Zenodo (14851275), code on GitHub, biokde.com web UI for academics; licence of the data not stated in the paper (article is CC BY-NC-ND).

projects.name: MedKGent (Zhang et al.; npj Digital Medicine)
projects.status: active (arXiv v3 Jul 2026; repo pushed 2026-06-19; Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.20759287)
projects.what_it_does: The only LLM-driven, confidence-aware KG over a large PubMed slice I found: 10M+ abstracts (1975-2023) with self-hosted Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct on 48 L20 GPUs. Extractor Agent: 50 stochastic samples per abstract at T=0.7, confidence = frequency (floored to 0.05), drop <0.6. Constructor Agent: recurring triple reinforces edge via s = 1-(1-s)(1-s'), appends PMIDs and refreshes timestamp; conflicting relation for the same pair is adjudicated by the LLM using confidence and date. Entities and the 12-type relation vocabulary come from PubTator3. Output 156k entities / 2.97M triples. Eval: LLM judges on 1% (34,725 abstracts, 83,438 triples) 85.4% (GPT-4.1) / 88.1% (DeepSeek-v3) 'valid'; two PhD annotators on 1,000 abstracts / 2,767 triples >86% valid, ~90% for most types.
projects.relevance_to_biolean: A worked example of three BioLean requirements: per-statement confidence, provenance (PMIDs, time), and aggregation across papers (same noisy-OR as iKraph). Also a warning: 'validity ~90%' is LLM/human-judged plausibility, not benchmark F1, and the 50-sample self-consistency makes it ~50x the cost of a single pass (hence 10M not 36M abstracts). Conflict handling (LLM picks a winner) is exactly the ambiguity problem Dan wants to keep explicit rather than resolve.
projects.reusable_assets: KG with confidences, timestamps, PMIDs on Hugging Face; code on GitHub; prompts.
key_refs: MedKGent: A Large Language Model Agent Framework for Constructing Temporally Evolving Medical Knowledge Graph, arXiv:2508.12393 (v3 Jul 2026), accepted npj Digital Medicine

projects.name: BioRelFact — joint relation + epistemic commitment (Keese et al., DFKI; LREC 2026)
projects.status: new (LREC 2026, pp 7592-7605); dataset described as public with code and prompts, but no repo located via GitHub search
projects.what_it_does: 1,767 expert-annotated biomedical sentences with 9 relation types and 5 levels of epistemic commitment (fact to hypothesis). Eight LLMs evaluated: GPT-OSS-20B best (F1 77.3 relation, 65.3 commitment), GPT-4o 75.9/60.2, Qwen3-8B-Thinking 74.6/57.2; definition-based few-shot prompts best; domain-adapted models mixed (MedGemma-27B +3.6/+4.4, Aloe-7B -4.3/-3.5). Error analysis ties confusions to specific hedging cues.
projects.relevance_to_biolean: The one benchmark that directly measures the thing Dan flagged as the open problem: how strongly does the sentence commit to the claim. ~0.65 F1 on 5 levels with an open 20B model means an epistemic field is extractable today but noisy; collapsing to 3 levels (asserted / hedged / negated) will be more reliable. Use its level scheme as the per-statement 'assertion strength' input to an evidence weight.

key_lessons: Fine-tuned encoders still beat prompted LLMs on strict relation schemas by a wide margin: PubTator3's BioREx+LinkBERT scores 82.0 F1 on BioRED, while frontier LLMs few-shot reach 0.11-0.31 F1 (Assi et al. 2026) and even fine-tuned GPT-3.5 (38.5) trails a specialised model (42.7) on relation+novelty (Lai et al. 2025). Use PubTator3's free relation2pubtator3 as the 28M-abstract backbone and spend LLM budget on the fields it lacks.

A second 'critic' pass is the cheapest precision lever: Claude 4.5 Sonnet went from 33.1% to 74.1% precision with a 92.6% false-positive cut on BioRED (Assi et al. 2026), and OntoGPT 1.2.0 added post-extraction term validation for the same reason. Recall did not improve; expect LLM annotation to be high-precision, low-recall.

Never let the model emit identifiers. Ungrounded GPT gave 1-3/100 correct GO/MONDO IDs; SPIRES with ontology lookup gave 97-98/100 (Caufield et al. 2024); an LLM used only as disambiguator over alias-match candidates adds up to +16 accuracy points (Ye & Mitchell, ACL 2025). Build a Gilda-style lexical index over the local 6M OBO terms and rerank with an LLM; do the same for predicates against RO/Biolink (RELATE 2025).

Both PubMed-scale weighted graphs that exist, iKraph (BERT-based, Nature MI 2025) and MedKGent (LLM-based, npj Digit Med 2026), aggregate evidence with the same noisy-OR, P = 1 - prod(1 - p_i), over mentions/papers, and both list source quality (journal, citations, date) as future work. This is the natural zero-order evidence score for a biolib lemma, and the obvious place for BioLean to add what they do not have: hedging, contradiction kept explicit, and formal semantics.

Hedging is extractable but noisy: 5-level epistemic commitment reaches 65.3 F1 with GPT-OSS-20B (BioRelFact, LREC 2026); the critic prompt's CORRECT/NEGATED/SPECULATIVE labels (Assi 2026) and RELATE's handling of implicit negation ('fails to affect') show the practical cut points. Store assertion strength as a first-class field, probably 3 levels, and feed it into the evidence weight.

Direction of effect and novelty are the hard labels, not entity pairs: BioCreative VIII best was 77 F1 for pairs but 59 for type, 59 for novelty and 45 for all together; direction annotation is reliable (IAA 90%) but the best model gets 37 F1 on relation+direction+novelty (Lai et al. 2025), and Association/Bind are inherently undirected. Dan's Ozempic chain needs 'inhibits', not 'associated with', so expect to hand-check direction for canonical statements.

Claim verification (SciFact-style SUPPORT/REFUTE/NEI) is a different and useful primitive: GPT-4 zero-shot ~0.79 label F1 and MultiVerS 0.73 on SciFact, but systems lose >=15 F1 on an open 500k-abstract corpus (SciFact-Open) and no gold standard exists for atomic-claim extraction (PaperTrail 2026). Use it to score a formal statement against retrieved abstracts (Dan has embeddings), not to build the graph.

Do not trust LLM-judged 'validity' as F1: judges were under 50% accurate on biomedical RE outputs until outputs were forced into a structured format (+15%) (Laskar et al., ACL 2025). MedKGent's ~90% validity and Assi's 0.31 F1 are measuring different things. BioLean's few hundred canonical papers should double as the human gold set.

Cost for 28.5M abstracts (about 400 input + ~500 output tokens each, cached schema prompt): Claude Haiku 5.5 at $0.10/$0.50 per MTok is roughly $9k list, ~$4.5k via the 50%-off Batch API; Sonnet 5.5 ~$165k/$83k; Opus 5.5 ~$330k/$165k; add ~1.5-2x for a critic pass. Open 8B weights on rented H100s ($2-4/GPU-h, ~4k tok/s measured) is ~1,000 GPU-hours, $2-5k; MedKGent's 32B model with 50-sample self-consistency took 48 GPUs and still stopped at 10M abstracts. The 112-core CPU box (~30 tok/s single stream for an 8B Q4 model) would take years for full PubMed but handles a few hundred canonical papers or a ~100k-abstract topic slice in days.

SemRep/SemMedDB, the classic triple source, was retired by NLM on 2024-12-31 (final dump 130M predications on May-2024 data); do not build on it, but its subject/predicate/object + UMLS CUI + sentence + PMID schema is still the most battle-tested shape for a referenced statement table.
open_questions: Recall vs precision: a proof needs the edge to exist, a weight needs the edge to be right. Does BioLean take PubTator3's high-recall correlation edges and let the LLM only annotate (direction, hedging, predicate type), or extract fresh with an LLM and accept ~0.3 recall?

How to encode epistemic strength formally: 5 BioRelFact levels, 3 critic labels, or a probability from noisy-OR aggregation? None of the surveyed systems map 'speculative' to a number in a principled way, and MedKGent resolves conflicts by letting the LLM pick a winner, which is the opposite of what Dan wants.

Novelty vs background: BioRED's novelty flag separates new findings from restated background; should restated background count as evidence of consensus (more weight) or be excluded to avoid double counting? No existing pipeline decides this.

Species: PubTator3 and iKraph ground genes to species-specific NCBI Gene IDs and no surveyed extractor maps mouse Glp1r to human GLP1R; BioLean needs an explicit orthology/translation layer before cross-species proofs are allowed.

Predicate vocabulary: PubTator3's 12 relation types (mostly correlations) vs RO/Biolink/BEL vs Dan's GO-typed 'copies (GO process)'. Which vocabulary do the Lean statements use, and is the RO->Lean mapping done once by hand or per statement by LLM+lookup (RELATE got only 52% exact match on predicates)?

Abstracts vs full text: ~74% of BioRED errors are cross-sentence and the mechanistic detail Dan wants is usually in Results, but PMC OA is only ~6M articles and full text is ~10x the tokens. Where is the cut?

Evaluation set: no benchmark covers grounded subject + RO predicate + direction + hedging + evidence sentence jointly; building the few-hundred-paper canonical set as a gold standard first (before any bulk run) seems necessary. Who annotates, and against which inter-annotator agreement target (direction got 90%)?

Self-consistency vs cheaper confidence: MedKGent's 50 samples per abstract gives calibrated-ish confidence at 50x cost; logprobs, a single critic pass, or agreement between two cheap models are untested alternatives at scale.

Data licences: iKraph's KG licence is unstated, MedKGent's Hugging Face set and PubTator3 bulk are open; the final SemMedDB dump has UMLS licence constraints. Which can be redistributed inside a public biolib?

projects.name: Nanopublication ecosystem (Knowledge Pixels: Nanopub Registry, Nanopub Query, Nanodash, nanopub-java, nanopub-py, trusty URIs, Knowledge Space trust model)
projects.status: active (2026). Registry/Query/Nanodash/nanopub-java all had commits on 2026-10-23; nanopub-py v2.2.2 released 2026-06-23; Knowledge Space spec v1.0 dated 2026-04-27. Company: Knowledge Pixels AG, Zurich (founded 2022, CEO Tobias Kuhn; advisors incl. Jan Velterop, Michel Dumontier), funded by BMV/acatech/NLnet, no visible revenue model.
projects.what_it_does: A nanopublication is a TriG named-graph bundle: assertion graph + provenance graph (PROV-O: prov:wasDerivedFrom, prov:wasAttributedTo) + pubinfo graph, identified by a content-hash 'trusty URI' (RA...) and RSA-signed. Second-generation infrastructure (2023-2026): Registry = key/value store + per-pubkey/per-type add-only lists with checksums, synced across 4 public instances (registry.knowledgepixels.com, nanodash.net, petapico.org, univie.ac.at); Query = RDF4J repos per type/pubkey with grlc-style named SPARQL queries; Nanodash = web UI with assertion templates and 'Spaces'. Trust model: a 'setting' nanopub names initial trusted agents; agents are added via endorsement chains (npx:approvesOf, npx:introduces) and get per-key quotas; trust scores recomputed every 10 min. Retraction/supersession are first-class (invalidation backlinks). Verified numbers on 2026-10-23: 95,503 signed nanopubs, 745 agents, 845 accounts in the new registry; the legacy nanopub-server network (np.knowledgepixels.com, server.np.dumontierlab.com) is still up with 10,946,717 nanopubs, of which ~95% are bulk DB dumps (DisGeNET 4.72M, neXtProt 4.01M, Human Protein Atlas 1.25M, WikiPathways 27k; NanoWeb table). A nanopub Agent Skill (knowledgepixels/nanopub-skill, SKILL.md for Claude Code/Codex etc.) wraps the nanopub-java CLI.
projects.relevance_to_biolean: The right container format for BioLean's 'formal, annotated, referenced statements': each literature-derived triple + PMID + ECO evidence type + annotator becomes one signed, immutable, hash-identified record; supersession/retraction model maps onto revising a biolib lemma. Dan can run his own Registry+Query via Docker Compose (localhost:9292/9393) and keep it private, or publish to the public network under one key (quota applies; registries refuse >1200 triples or >1MB per nanopub, so one statement per nanopub). Sceptical read: (1) the registry's trust model is about WHO may publish (endorsement chains), not about HOW TRUE a claim is; it gives BioLean nothing for evidence weighting. (2) There is no existing corpus of literature-derived formal biology claims to reuse: the 10.9M legacy nanopubs are DB re-serialisations, and the 95k signed ones are mostly templates, FAIR metadata, reviews and social-science claims (type list shows ECO_0000361, OBI, SIO, cito:supports/disputes, hycl#AIDA-Sentence, superpattern terms, but no gene/disease templates). (3) No reasoning layer at all; nanopubs are storage/attribution only.

projects.name: Super-pattern and 'formalization papers' (Bucur, Kuhn, Ceolin, van Ossenbruggen; VU Amsterdam / CWI)
projects.status: maintained but quiet (2023). Field study published 2023-02-21; the superpattern vocabulary (w3id.org/linkflows/superpattern/terms/...) is live in the Nanopub Query type list in 2026 and a Nanodash template exists; no new papers found 2024-2026.
projects.what_it_does: Analysed the main claims of a cross-discipline sample of papers and found they do not fit plain RDF/OWL triples. Proposed a 5-slot template with a formal first-order semantics: CONTEXT class, SUBJECT class, QUALIFIER, RELATION, OBJECT class. Qualifiers have defined meanings: 'generally' = in at least 90% of instances, 'mostly', 'frequently', 'sometimes', 'can', 'never', 'always'; relations are a small closed set (causes, contributes to, enables, prevents, inhibits, requires, affects, is same as...). Example: 'in the context of rat brain endothelial cells, transient oxidative stress generally causes tight-junction disruption'. Each formalisation is itself a nanopublication linked to the paper it formalises. The 2023 field study ran a real special issue (Data Science, IOS Press) of 15 'formalization papers' by 18 authors, with submissions, reviews and decisions all as nanopubs; authors found it feasible but the UI technical. Also builds on Kuhn 2013 'AIDA sentences' (Atomic, Independent, Declarative, Absolute English sentences as a fallback for claims not yet formalisable) and meta-nanopubs expressing agreement/disagreement.
projects.relevance_to_biolean: The closest existing attempt at exactly Dan's step 1 ('annotate the statements in canonical publications with ontology terms'). It shows the triple 'DNApol copies DNA' is too weak: real claims need a context slot (cell type, organism, condition) and a quantified qualifier, and the qualifier semantics ('generally' = >=90%) is what makes an Ozempic-style chain (inhibits -> responsible for breakdown -> reduces hunger) evaluable. The closed relation set and class-based (not instance-based) subjects map cleanly onto Lean structures. Caveat: the formal semantics was defined but never executed by any reasoner; nobody chained super-pattern claims into derivations. Their qualifier set is also coarse for biology (no dose, no tissue specificity beyond context).

projects.name: Cardinal assertions (Gibson, van Dam, Schultes, Roos, Mons 2012) and Knowlets / WikiProteins / Concept Web Alliance / ConceptWiki (Mons 2008-2012)
projects.status: dead as software (last activity ~2012; wikiprofessional.org and ConceptWiki gone, Knewco defunct, no GitHub). Ideas live on only in papers and in PROV-K 2025.
projects.what_it_does: Knowlets (Mons et al. 2008, Genome Biology): a 'concept profile' that records the relationship between two concepts ONCE and accumulates three weights as evidence grows: F (number of factual statements from curated DBs like UniProt/GO/IntAct), C (sentence co-occurrence count in PubMed), A (indirect association). >1M concept Knowlets built over UMLS/Swiss-Prot/GO; the point was that the 'concept space' grows minimally while the 'text space' explodes. WikiProteins was the community-annotation wiki on top (Bairoch, Ashburner, Jimmy Wales co-authors); never left beta. Cardinal assertions (Gibson et al., SWAT4LS 2012, position paper): 'the result of aggregating the evidence associated with identical assertions to produce a new measure that represents a consensus of that evidence', with two hard criteria: (1) it links to every component nanopublication, (2) 'the method of generating the overall confidence score should be clearly defined and linked to'. Cardinal assertions are themselves immutable nanopubs; new evidence produces a new edition, giving a versioned chain of the evidence state over time. Cites STRING combined scores and neXtProt gold/silver/bronze as the practical precedents. The W3C HCLS wiki classes 'textbook' cardinal assertions (e.g. 'malaria is caused by mosquitoes') as the broadly accepted universals.
projects.relevance_to_biolean: This IS Dan's KEY REQUIREMENT, stated in 2012 and never built: a biolib lemma is a cardinal assertion (consensus statement + evidence score + links to supporting nanopubs + the scoring method itself published and citable + versioned as evidence changes). Knowlets' F/C/A split is a ready-made decomposition for an evidence score: curated-DB facts (Dan's GOA/UniProt), text co-occurrence (PubTator3/Open Targets europepmc sentences), inferred association. Why it failed: it was a position paper with no implementation; Knowlets were proprietary (Knewco) and co-occurrence-based rather than claim-based. Nothing to install; everything to copy in design.

projects.name: PROV-K / Provenance-Driven Nanopublications (Menotti, Marchesin, Giachelle, Silvello; University of Padova)
projects.status: active (2025). IRCDL Feb 2025 workshop paper (CEUR Vol-3937 paper 10) expanded to IJDL journal article 2025; PDF modified 2025-09-13.
projects.what_it_does: Extends the nanopub model with a fourth 'knowledge provenance' named graph for assertions that come from aggregating several sources (an IE system, a truth-discovery step). PROV-K is a PROV-O extension that represents each piece of evidence as supporting OR conflicting with the assertion, carries truth values/reliability scores, and defines trust relationships agent->agent and agent->proposition. Applied at scale: 197,511 gene-expression/cancer associations from CoreKB (CORE relation-extraction system) serialised as extended nanopubs and released on Zenodo; a second use case builds a trust network over 45,649 facts using three LLM agents as assessors and measures how well LLMs judge trustworthiness.
projects.relevance_to_biolean: The only implemented, recent (2025) version of the cardinal-assertion idea, and it handles the OPEN PROBLEM Dan named: conflicting evidence is represented explicitly in the same graph as supporting evidence, with per-source reliability, instead of being collapsed into one number. The TriG serialisation (Figure 1 of the paper) is a template for BioLean's aggregated-evidence layer. Also the only prior art for 'LLM as a trust agent' in this space, with an accuracy evaluation; useful as a warning and a baseline. Limits: PROV-K is a provenance vocabulary, not a scoring theory; their truth values come from CORE's own aggregation; the nanopubs live on the Padova server, not the public registry.

projects.name: SEPIO (Scientific Evidence and Provenance Information Ontology) -> SEPIO-LinkML -> GA4GH VA-Spec (Statement / Proposition / EvidenceLine)
projects.status: active in its LinkML/GA4GH form (sepio-linkml pushed 2026-10-14; ga4gh/va-spec 1.1.0 released 2026-10-02). The OWL ontology on OBO Foundry is stale: last release 2023-06-13 and its README warns it is 'out of date' and to use the LinkML repo instead.
projects.what_it_does: Matt Brush's (Monarch/ClinGen) evidence model, now the backbone of GA4GH Variant Annotation spec. Core split: Proposition = 'an abstract entity representing a possible fact that is either true or false' (the thing you prove); Statement = 'a claim of truth made by a particular agent on a particular occasion' about a Proposition, with direction (supports / disputes / neutral), strength, score, negated, subjectClassification; EvidenceLine = 'an evidence-based argument that may support or refute a target proposition' with directionOfEvidenceProvided, strengthOfEvidenceProvided, scoreOfEvidenceProvided and hasEvidenceItems; Method and Agent for how/who. Shortcut slots hasEvidence / hasEvidenceOfTypes (ECO) when you skip evidence lines. Profiles (ClinGen-ACMG variant pathogenicity) show it used in production clinical curation. Biolink Model (which Dan's sibling project already exports) borrowed the same ideas: has_evidence (ECO), knowledge_level, agent_type on Associations.
projects.relevance_to_biolean: The cleanest existing data model for the thing BioLean must get right: keep the formal Proposition (a Lean term) separate from the many Statements/EvidenceLines about it, each with direction and strength, so competing hypotheses are just two Statements with opposite direction on one Proposition and 'how established' is a fold over EvidenceLines. ClinGen proves this works for real curation with weighted evidence (ACMG criteria strengths). Because it is LinkML, Dan gets Python dataclasses, JSON Schema and RDF for free (uv add linkml), and it round-trips to his existing KGX/Biolink export. Caveats: VA-Spec is variant-centric; the generic SEPIO LinkML core has no profiles yet and no stated maintainer/version on its docs page; strength/score are free-form, so the scoring function is still Dan's.
projects.reusable_assets: sepio-linkml schema (w3id.org/sepio-framework/sepio-linkml) with generated artefacts; GA4GH VA-Spec 1.1.0 (schema + Python reference implementation); ClinGen-ACMG SEPIO profile as a worked example of evidence-strength weighting; legacy SEPIO OWL (purl.obolibrary.org/obo/sepio.owl, 2023) already in Dan's OBO dump.

projects.status: ECO active (release v2026-07-10; prior releases 2026-05-15, 2025-04-30, 2024-07-19; CC0; NSF funding ended, maintained by UMD/IGS). ECO-CollecTF: one-off corpus 2021, archived. CIO: draft, dormant (last push 2025-02-03; paper 2015; near-zero adoption outside Bgee).
projects.what_it_does: ECO types evidence and assertion methods (~1,900 native terms; 3,340 classes incl. imports in 2025-04-30 release): e.g. ECO:0000269 experimental evidence used in manual assertion, ECO:0000315 mutant phenotype, ECO:0000250 sequence similarity, ECO:0007669 computational evidence used in automatic assertion. ECO deliberately does NOT rank or weight evidence. ECO-CollecTF (Hobbs, Erill et al. 2021): 84 open-access papers, 2,565 sentence/sentence-pair annotations linking an experimental-evidence statement to a biological assertion, labelled with 146 ECO terms plus negation, ECO-selection confidence and ASSERTION STRENGTH ratings; >=3 curators per doc, Cohen's kappa 0.69; BRAT/BioC, CC BY-NC. CIO (Bastian, Chibucos, Gaudet, Giglio, Lewis, Orchard, Poux, Robinson-Rechavi et al. 2015) tried to standardise confidence: 'high/medium/low confidence from single evidence', 'congruent' vs 'conflicting' multiple evidence lines, 'has greater confidence than' relations, with evidence types from ECO. projects.relevance_to_biolean: Dan already has ECO in his OBO dump and ECO codes on every GOA annotation and UniProt evidence tag, so evidence TYPE is free; the missing piece is a type->weight function, and the history says: ECO refused to define one, CIO tried a generic one and nobody adopted it, while resource-specific ones (STRING scores, neXtProt gold/silver/bronze, ClinGen ACMG strengths) are what people actually use. So BioLean should define its own explicit, published weighting over ECO types (plus replication count and source) rather than wait for a standard. ECO-CollecTF is the only existing corpus that does precisely Dan's step 1 (sentence-level annotation of 'statement + evidence type + strength' in papers) and is a ready test set and annotation-guideline template; note it annotates Results sections of full text, whereas Dan mostly has abstracts.

projects.name: Micropublications ontology (Clark, Ciccarese, Goble) + Domeo / Annotation Ontology

projects.what_it_does: An argumentation model for biomedical claims, explicitly 'intended to complement the more narrowly focused nanopublication model'. Minimal form: a Statement plus attribution. Maximal form: Claims supported by Data, Methods, Materials; Statements that mp:supports / mp:challenges other statements; Representations (quotes, figures) anchored in articles; qualifiers and formalisations of the same claim; discussion and disagreement as first-class objects. Grounded in Toulmin-style argumentation theory. The Harvard/MGH team also produced the Annotation Ontology (AO) that fed into W3C Open Annotation / Web Annotation Data Model.
projects.relevance_to_biolean: Supplies the piece nanopubs lack: claims arguing with other claims. For Dan's ambiguity problem, mp:supports/mp:challenges between Statements (with each Statement anchored to a text span + PMID) is the graph you need before any evidence score can be computed; the citation chain analysis in the paper (claims citing claims that cite nothing) is also a good argument for BioLean's 'referenced statements' rule. key_lessons: Keep the Proposition separate from the Statements about it. SEPIO/GA4GH VA-Spec (1.1.0, Oct 2026) model a Proposition as the abstract possible-fact and each curator/paper/DB contribution as a Statement or EvidenceLine with direction (supports/disputes), strength and score. For BioLean that means the Lean term is the Proposition and 'how established' is a fold over EvidenceLines; competing hypotheses are just opposite-direction Statements on one Proposition, not two different facts.

Evidence type is solved; evidence weight is not, and nobody will solve it for you. ECO (release 2026-07-10) deliberately only types evidence and is already on every GOA/UniProt record Dan has; CIO (2015) tried a generic confidence scale and never got adopted; what people actually use are resource-specific functions (STRING combined score, neXtProt gold/silver/bronze, ClinGen ACMG strengths). BioLean should publish its own explicit ECO-type x replication x source weighting and, per Gibson et al. 2012, make the scoring method itself a citable, linked artefact.

The biolib lemma already has a name: cardinal assertion (Gibson, van Dam, Schultes, Roos, Mons, SWAT4LS 2012). Aggregate identical assertions into one consensus with an evidence value, link every component nanopub, link the method, treat it as immutable and issue new editions as evidence changes. It was never built between 2012 and PROV-K 2025, which is the gap BioLean fills.

Real claims need a context slot and a quantified qualifier. The super-pattern study (Bucur, Kuhn et al., K-CAP 2021; PeerJ CS 2023) found plain triples cannot carry main claims and used CONTEXT + SUBJECT + QUALIFIER ('generally' = >=90%, 'frequently', 'sometimes', 'never') + closed RELATION set + OBJECT. The Ozempic chain only evaluates if 'inhibits' and 'reduces hunger' carry qualifiers; adopt that template, and use AIDA sentences (Kuhn 2013) as the fallback for claims not yet formalisable.

Represent conflict explicitly instead of averaging it away. Micropublications (Clark, Ciccarese, Goble 2014) make mp:supports/mp:challenges first-class edges between statements; PROV-K (Menotti et al. 2025) stores supporting and conflicting evidence with per-source reliability in the same graph for 197k gene-cancer assertions; CIO distinguishes congruent from conflicting evidence lines. A proof system can then expose 'contested' as a state rather than a low score.

Registry trust is about agents, not claims. The 2025-26 Nanopub Registry computes trust from endorsement chains between signing keys and uses it for publishing quotas; it says nothing about whether an assertion is true. Reuse it for 'who may contribute to biolib', never as an evidence weight.

There is no reusable corpus of formal literature claims in biology. The legacy nanopub network's 10.9M nanopubs are ~95% DB re-serialisations (DisGeNET 4.7M, neXtProt 4.0M, HPA 1.25M); the new signed registry has 95,503 nanopubs, almost none biological. The only sentence-level 'statement + ECO evidence type + strength' corpus is ECO-CollecTF (84 papers, 2,565 annotations, Zenodo 2021), useful as a test set and guideline template. Dan's raw material (PubTator3 BioREx relations, Open Targets europepmc sentences, GOA PMID links) is already richer than anything in this angle.

Platforms die, standards-shaped files survive. Knowlets/ConceptWiki (2012), Domeo and purl.org/mp (2014-16), Open PHACTS (Foundation dissolved 2025-02-18) all vanished with funding; ECO, PROV-O, W3C Web Annotation and the nanopub guidelines (moved to a community repo) persisted. Store BioLean statements as plain TriG/parquet with content-hash IDs and PROV-O provenance, optionally mirrored to a self-hosted Nanopub Registry (Docker Compose, localhost:9292), rather than inside any one platform.

Anchor every statement to the exact text span. W3C Web Annotation selectors (TextQuoteSelector exact/prefix/suffix + PMID/DOI) as used by Hypothesis make annotations portable and re-anchorable to full text later; SciBot shows the workable loop of machine-proposed, human-verified annotations. Use the selector, not the Hypothesis service, as the dependency.

Identifier equivalence is a parameter, not a fact. Open PHACTS 'scientific lenses' let one query treat semaglutide and its salts (or gene/protein/ortholog) as equivalent and another not. BioLean proofs will need the same: which CHEBI/UniProt/HGNC equivalences a derivation assumed must be recorded with the proof.
open_questions: Publish to the public Nanopub Registry (citability, interop, one signing key with quota) or run a private registry/plain TriG store with the same shape and publish only biolib-level cardinal assertions? The registry's per-key quota and 1200-triple/1MB limits suit one-statement-per-nanopub but not bulk imports of 1.28M GOA links.

How do super-pattern qualifiers ('generally' = >=90%, 'frequently', 'sometimes', 'never') map into Lean: a probabilistic/weighted logic, a threshold that promotes a Proposition to a classical Prop once its evidence score passes it, or both (dual encoding)?

What is the evidence-score function exactly, and is it itself a versioned nanopub? Candidates from this angle: Knowlet-style F (curated-DB facts, by ECO type) / C (text-mined sentence support, from PubTator3 and Open Targets europepmc) / A (inferred), combined per Gibson's criteria (method linked, components linked, new edition on change).

Should competing hypotheses be two Statements with opposite direction on one Proposition (SEPIO), an argument graph of mp:supports/mp:challenges between statements (micropublications), or PROV-K-style supporting/conflicting evidence inside one aggregated assertion? These give different proof semantics for 'contested'.

Dan has abstracts, not full text: is a TextQuoteSelector on the abstract sentence a sufficient anchor, and how should the ECO-CollecTF guidelines (written for Results sections) be adapted to abstract-level evidence statements?

PROV-K used LLMs as trust agents and measured their accuracy. Should LLM-derived statements enter BioLean's evidence pool at all, and if so with what ECO type (ECO:0007669 automatic assertion) and what prior weight, so they cannot inflate 'established' scores?

Which identifier lenses (CHEBI parent/salt/conjugate, UniProt isoform/ortholog, HGNC gene vs protein) must a proof record as assumptions, and can those be expressed as Lean typeclass instances rather than per-proof flags?

projects.name: INDRA (Integrated Network and Dynamical Reasoning Assembler)
projects.status: active (release 1.24.0 2025-07-30; commits to 2026-06-30; 230 stars)
projects.what_it_does: Python library that turns reader output and curated DBs into typed Statements (Phosphorylation, Activation/Inhibition, IncreaseAmount/DecreaseAmount, Complex, Translocation, ActiveForm, Conversion, Gef/Gap...). Agents carry db_refs (HGNC, UP, FPLX, CHEBI, GO, MESH...). Each Statement has an Evidence list: source_api, pmid, sentence text, epistemics {direct, negated, hypothesis}, text_refs, and reader annotations (e.g. REACH rule name in found_by). Preassembler: combine_duplicates (by matches_key), combine_related (builds a refinement partial order using FamPlex/GO/CHEBI isa/partof; a Statement refines another if more specific on >=1 element and equal elsewhere), find_contradicts (polarity pairs only: Activation vs Inhibition, IncreaseAmount vs DecreaseAmount, Phosphorylation vs Dephosphorylation). BeliefEngine: per-source systematic error e_syst and random error e_rand; P(wrong) = product over sources of (e_syst_s + product over that source's evidences of e_rand_s); belief = 1 - P(wrong). Defaults: readers e_rand 0.3 / e_syst 0.05; curated DBs e_rand 0.01-0.2 / e_syst 0.01; GNBR e_syst 0.1. Hierarchy belief: a general Statement inherits evidence from all more-specific Statements that refine it; evidence never flows the other way. indra.belief.skl has trainable CountsScorer/HybridScorer. Assemblers in master: pysb (-> SBML, BNGL, Kappa via PySB), sbgn (PD), pybel, cx/cyjs (NDEx), sif, indranet, graph, english, html (curation UI), index_card, kami, tsv. No BioPAX assembler: BioPAX is input-only (pybiopax). No evidence any INDRA/EMMAA model was deposited to BioModels. Verified: the MSB 2023 paper (Bachman, Gyori, Sorger) processed 567,507 articles -> 5.9M raw reader Statements + 730k from DBs -> 2.9M after filtering -> ~900k unique; 63% single-evidence; 38% of Statements refine another; 19% of Statements have >=2 readers; single-mention precision by reader: RLIMS-P 80%, TRIPS 79%, MedScan 66%, REACH 48%, Sparser 36%; overall 73% of 1,800 curated Statements correct; random forest belief model AUPRC 0.942 vs 0.893 for counts-only.

Reuse directly: Statement JSON schema as the intermediate representation; the refinement partial order (subsumption via ontology) as the model for 'general claim is supported by specific claims'; the two-error belief model and the specific->general evidence-flow rule as the starting edge weight; find_contradicts as the detector of competing claims. key_lessons: Separate two kinds of 'how established': extraction reliability and scientific consensus. INDRA's belief (MSB 2023) is almost entirely the first; the authors found most wrong Statements come from grounding, polarity, negation and hypothesis errors, not from the literature disagreeing. BioLean needs both numbers on every edge.

Steal INDRA's statement model, not its readers: typed relation + grounded agents + an Evidence list with source, PMID, sentence and epistemics flags. The JSON Schema exists (indra/resources/statements_schema.json). Extend relation types to GO process / SO rather than inventing a new container.

Refinement as a partial order is the right primitive. INDRA builds a lattice from ontology isa/partof (38% of Statements refine another) and lets evidence flow only from specific to general. In Lean this is a subsumption relation plus a monotone evidence-aggregation lemma; INDRA already shows it scales to ~1M statements.

Use noisy-OR with per-source systematic + random error as the baseline weight (INDRA default_belief_probs.json: readers 0.3/0.05, curated DBs 0.01-0.2/0.01). A trained model beat it (AUPRC 0.942 vs 0.893) once ~1,800 curated statements existed, so plan a curation loop with INDRA's 12 error tags (correct, entity_boundaries, grounding, no_relation, wrong_relation, act_vs_amt, polarity, negative_result, hypothesis, agent_conditions, mod_site, other).

Independent extractors agreeing is the strongest cheap signal: 81% of INDRA relations came from one reader, pairwise correlations were 0.03-0.63, and multi-reader support predicted correctness. Dan has three independent extractions locally (PubTator3 BioREx, Open Targets EuropePMC, INDRA Statement export); count agreement as a feature.

EMMAA is the existing 'proof' engine and it is just bounded path search in a signed graph with an English witness (INDRA ModelChecker, codes PATHS_FOUND / NO_PATHS_FOUND / MAX_PATH_LENGTH_EXCEEDED). It never composes belief along the path or across alternative paths, and the authors say causal transitivity is unresolved. That gap is BioLean's contribution: a Lean proof of 'semaglutide reduces hunger' is a chain of edge lemmas whose belief is composed by explicit rules.

Contradictions: INDRA only detects polarity opposites (find_contradicts) and leaves resolution to 'context, functional data, or ensembles'. Nobody in this ecosystem has a formal treatment of competing hypotheses, so do not expect to import one.

Self-updating knowledge dies with its grant: EMMAA models froze on 2024-08-01, within months of DARPA ASKE ending, though the site still serves. BioLean should be a reproducible batch build from the local data, with versioned releases like mathlib, not a daily pipeline on AWS.

Export targets are a distraction for a proof project. INDRA offers PySB->SBML/BNGL/Kappa, SBGN-PD, PyBEL, CX and SIF, but no BioPAX export and no BioModels deposits; dynamical export needs hand-supplied rates. Lean is the target; keep INDRA Statement JSON as the exchange format and emit SBGN/SBML only for figures.

The grounding stack is alive and reusable: Gilda 1.6.1 (June 2026) grounds 'semaglutide' to CHEBI:167574 in one call; Bioregistry normalises CURIEs; SeMRA (Bioinformatics 2025) is a small existing example of inference over mappings with a confidence per inferred edge, including code.

The lab's 2026 direction is LLM-as-curator (indra-belief-model: gemma-4-26b judges each Statement/Evidence pair with a disconfirm-first prompt, with a calibration profile per model+prompt). Record provenance of every weight the same way, because weights from different judges are not comparable.
open_questions: Can a bulk INDRA DB dump (preassembled Statements with belief and evidence) be obtained for local use, or must BioLean rebuild from the sibling project's INDRA Statement JSON export? Which readers/sources does that export actually contain?
How should belief compose in Lean along a proof: product along a path, noisy-OR across independent paths, and what counts as independent when two paths share a PMID? INDRA/EMMAA never answered this.
Which formal logic fits competing hypotheses with weights (Dempster-Shafer, probabilistic argumentation, paraconsistent)? INDRA offers only polarity-contradiction detection as input.
Is the INDRA Statement class hierarchy or MIRA's typed template schema the better starting point for a Lean inductive type of biological statements that must also cover GO processes and SO features?
How many curations exist in INDRA DB and can they be downloaded to bootstrap BioLean's evidence model and its error taxonomy?
Can an LLM judge like indra-belief-model run usefully on 112 CPU cores without a GPU, or should BioLean budget for an API model for the evidence-check step over a few hundred canonical papers?
Gilda is built from INDRA's bio_ontology (molecular + GO/MeSH/disease); how much work is it to load the 6.0M OBO terms (SO, PATO, UBERON, ECO) into Gilda's grounder format?
Should ECO (Evidence and Conclusion Ontology) codes, already attached to GOA annotations, be the evidence-type vocabulary for BioLean rather than INDRA's source_api strings?

projects.what_it_does: Nemo is a Rust Datalog engine (stratified negation, aggregates, existential rules, RDF/CSV/SPARQL input) with a CLI `--trace` / `--trace-all-idb-facts` option that exports derivation traces. CertifyingDatalog is a Lean 4 checker, formally verified against Datalog least-model and proof-theoretic semantics, that accepts those traces as JSON proof trees or DAGs and certifies each step. ITP 2025 paper: checking 1000 GALEN (EL ontology) conclusions took 0.2-0.4 s; DAG format keeps proofs small (4-10 MB) where trees blow up (313 MB on the exponential case). The repo's Examples/elReasoning encodes an EL consequence-based calculus as Nemo rules (el-calc.rls) and checks the resulting ontology-classification proofs in Lean; a companion DL 2025 paper (arXiv 2507.21851) does the same for three EL calculi and translates Nemo traces back into DL proofs.
projects.relevance_to_biolean: This is the 'Datalog engine finds the derivation, Lean checks it' architecture already built and verified: BioLean's literature statements become EDB facts, RO/GO rules become Nemo rules, Nemo answers 'semaglutide reduces hunger?' and emits a trace, Lean certifies it. Limits: the verified checker covers positive, function-free, safe Datalog only (Nemo's negation/existentials/aggregates are not certified); no weights (the checker verifies structure, so evidence scores must be recomputed by a separate Lean function over the certified tree); the Nemo->checker conversion scripts (inputCreatorNemo.py) target Nemo 0.7.1 trace format and must be retested against 0.10.x. Decidability: PTIME data complexity. Reuse this rather than writing a Lean Datalog checker from scratch.
projects.reusable_assets: Lean 4 library + executable (Apache-2.0/MIT); JSON proof-tree and ordered-DAG formats; Nemo CLI/Python/WASM bindings (Apache-2.0/MIT); EL-calculus-as-rules example (el-calc.rls) directly applicable to OBO ontologies

projects.name: Ubergraph + relation-graph + Whelk + ELK + ROBOT (OBO reasoning stack)
projects.status: active - Ubergraph commits 2026-10-02 and SPARQL endpoint answered a live aggregate query in 20 s on 2026-10-23; relation-graph v2.3.4 2026-03-13; Whelk v1.2.1 2024-09-30 (commit 2025-03); ELK 0.6.0 2024-05-25 (last commit 2024-07, maintained not active); ROBOT v1.9.11 2026-10-01
projects.what_it_does: Ubergraph merges 41 OBO ontologies (GO, CHEBI, MONDO, UBERON, CL, PATO, NCBITaxon, RO...), classifies with `robot reason -r ELK`, materialises all entailed existential relations with relation-graph (built on Whelk, an OWL EL+RL reasoner in Scala), and serves it from Blazegraph at https://ubergraph.apps.renci.org/sparql. Named graphs: `ontology` (asserted+classified axioms, labels, information-content scores), `redundant` (full closure), `nonredundant` (closure minus redundant edges). My probe of the nonredundant graph: 46,379 part_of (BFO:0000050), 2,909 regulates (RO:0002211), 2,567 positively regulates (RO:0002213), 3 causally upstream of (RO:0002411) class-level edges. Whelk paper: ELK classifies Ubergraph in 99 s vs Whelk 40 min, but Whelk answers 90M DL queries in <8 h where ELK would need >400 days; ELK 0.6.0 added proof-generation hooks (Protege proof plugins). ROBOT provides `reason`, `explain`, `relax`, `reduce`, `materialize`.
projects.relevance_to_biolean: BioLean should treat the OBO layer as a precomputed fact base, not run an OWL reasoner: download the nonredundant edge tables (integer-indexed edges.tsv + node-labels.tsv) and load into DuckDB/Nemo as EDB facts; ontology axioms carry weight 1 (definitional) while literature edges carry evidence weights. Expressiveness: OWL 2 EL (PTIME) for classes, RL for individuals; no confidences anywhere in the stack (information-content scores are frequency, not evidence). ROBOT `explain` gives justifications (sets of axioms), not proof trees - so for Lean checking, re-derive via Nemo's EL rules rather than importing ELK/Whelk output. Chris Mungall and Jim Balhoff are the people behind both this and GO-CAM.

projects.name: Relation Ontology (RO) - OBO relations and their OWL semantics
projects.status: active - release v2026-09-04, commits 2026-10-05; local copy at /home/danbolser/Work/IUK-IPF/data/sources/ontology/raw/ro.obo is release 2025-12-17
projects.what_it_does: The shared predicate vocabulary for OBO and GO-CAM. Local ro.obo: 704 typedefs, 45 transitive, 121 inverse pairs, 38 transitive_over, 102 holds_over_chain (sub-property chain) axioms, 0 equivalent_to_chain. Causal module: `causally upstream of` (RO:0002411, transitive), `regulates` (RO:0002211) and +/- variants, `directly positively regulates`, `enables` (RO:0002327), `acts upstream of` := enables o causally upstream of (RO:0002264), `involved in regulation of` := enables o regulates, `capable of regulating` := capable of o regulates, `has input/has output`, `provides input for`. Everything is within OWL 2 EL (regular property chains), so ELK/Whelk/Nemo-EL-rules handle it; no uncertainty or weights.
projects.relevance_to_biolean: RO is where BioLean's statement predicates should come from ('DNApol (enables GO:0003887) ... copies DNA' maps to enables / has input / has output, not a new verb). The 102 chain axioms are literally Horn rules and are the natural first contents of biolib: e.g. `enables(P,F) ∧ causally_upstream_of(F,Q) → acts_upstream_of(P,Q)`, each provable as a Lean lemma once RO's OWL semantics are stated. Caveats: 704 relations with many near-synonyms is an ambiguity source (GO-CAM restricts itself to ~20); RO chains are one-directional entailments (sub-property), so you cannot decompose a coarse statement back into fine ones; RO says nothing about evidence - weights have to live on BioLean's instance-level edges, not on RO axioms.

projects.name: GO-CAM / Noctua / Minerva / Arachne (Gene Ontology causal activity models)
projects.status: active models (noctua-models commit 2026-10-23; go-shapes commit 2026-10-08); Minerva server commits 2026-10-19 but last release v0.6.3 2024-11; Arachne reasoner dormant (last commit 2023-05, release v1.2.1 2020-01)
projects.what_it_does: GO-CAMs are OWL 2 ABoxes: each node is an OWL individual typed by a GO/CHEBI/UBERON class, edges are RO causal relations between molecular activities (`directly provides input for`, `directly positively regulates`, `causally upstream of`...), and every edge/annotation carries an ECO evidence code plus a reference (PMID). Minerva (OWL API + Blazegraph wrapper) is the server; Arachne (Scala Rete-based OWL RL rule engine) was built to give sub-second real-time inference inside Noctua; Whelk now also supports GO-CAM ABox reasoning in ROBOT/Protege. Models are published as Turtle in noctua-models, via the GO SPARQL endpoint (rdf.geneontology.org), the gocam-py LinkML schema/JSON, and the GO-CAM browser.
projects.relevance_to_biolean: The closest existing instance of Dan's 'formal, annotated, referenced statement': (activity_A, RO:directly_positively_regulates, activity_B, ECO:0000314, PMID:x). BioLean should adopt this shape (and ECO as the evidence-type axis for weighting) instead of inventing one, and can bootstrap its baseline from thousands of curated GO-CAMs plus the 1.28M GOA annotation->PMID links already on disk. What it lacks is exactly BioLean's goal: no weighting beyond ECO class, no aggregation of multiple references into a confidence, no higher-level derived claims, and reasoning is OWL RL materialisation (Arachne/Whelk) with no proof objects. Arachne's dormancy shows the GO stack converged on Whelk.

projects.name: BioASP / clingo tools: iggy, caspo, meneco (+ plingo for probabilities)
projects.status: clingo active (v5.8.2 2026-08-14); caspo maintained (v4.0.3 2026-02-10, but CHANGES shows last scientific change 4.0.0 in 2020: Python 3 + clingo 5); iggy dormant (v2.2.0 2021-08, commit 2022-01); meneco dormant (v2.0.2 2022-04); plingo dormant (v1.1.0 2023-04, commit 2024-06)
projects.what_it_does: Potsdam/Rennes answer-set-programming tools for biological networks. iggy: sign-consistency between an influence graph (CIF) and observed up/down changes; reports minimal inconsistent cores, minimal repairs, and strong/weak predictions for unmeasured nodes. caspo: learns families of Boolean signalling models from phospho-proteomics data (reported 11,700 models compatible with one liver-cell dataset once error is allowed for), then designs discriminating experiments and intervention strategies. meneco: metabolic network gap-filling by minimal reaction additions. plingo adds LPMLN/ProbLog/P-log probabilistic semantics on top of clingo (weighted rules, MAP and marginal inference via optimisation/enumeration).
projects.relevance_to_biolean: ASP is the mature answer to Dan's open problem of competing hypotheses: a stable model is a consistent world, the set of answer sets is 'what the literature is consistent with', minimal inconsistent cores localise contradictions, and weak constraints/plingo weights rank worlds by evidence. Decidability: finite ground programs; NP (normal) / Sigma-2-P (disjunctive); clingo scales to millions of ground rules. The catch for Lean: ASP conclusions are non-monotonic, so there is no proof tree to certify - you can cheaply check in Lean that a given interpretation is a stable model (polynomial for normal programs), but not certify 'X holds in every answer set' without re-solving. Design implication: use ASP for hypothesis enumeration/repair, keep the certified Lean layer for the monotone (Datalog) part. The biology tools themselves are mostly unmaintained; the engine and the modelling patterns are what to take.

projects.name: Weighted / probabilistic logic programming: ProbLog, PyReason, Scallop, semiring provenance
projects.status: ProbLog active (v2.3.0 2026-09-09); PyReason active (v4.0.0b4 2026-10-19); Scallop maintained (release 0.2.4 2024-08, commits 2026-06); semiring-provenance theory is settled literature (2007, KR 2022)
projects.what_it_does: ProbLog: Prolog clauses with independent probabilities; query probability via knowledge compilation (BDD/SDD); its founding application (IJCAI 2007) was link discovery in Biomine, a probabilistic biological KG - so 'weighted edges in a bio KG under logic' is a 19-year-old idea. PyReason (ASU Lab V2): generalised annotated logic over graphs with [lower,upper] interval truth values, temporal steps, open-world reasoning and explainable inference traces; lists biological networks as a target. Scallop (PLDI 2023): Datalog with recursion/negation/aggregation whose engine is parameterised by a provenance semiring (max-min, top-k proofs, differentiable). Semiring provenance (Green-Karvounarakis-Tannen 2007) is the general theory: annotate facts, propagate through joins (product) and alternative derivations (sum); Viterbi semiring gives 'confidence of the best derivation'; Bourgaux et al. (KR 2022) fix the infinite-derivation problem under recursion.
projects.relevance_to_biolean: This is the canonical machinery for Dan's KEY REQUIREMENT. Define the evidence weight of a derived claim as a semiring value computed over its certified proof tree: product (or min) along a chain, sum (or max) across independent supports. Because CertifyingDatalog already hands Lean the proof tree, scoring is a pure Lean function over that tree - mathlib has the semiring algebra - and both structure and score are checked. Pitfalls learned here: ProbLog's independence assumption overcounts literature evidence (one experiment cited by 50 papers is not 50 supports), so BioLean needs a dedup/independence model before probabilities mean anything; inference in ProbLog is #P-hard (fine for hundreds of statements, not millions); PyReason's interval annotations are a cheap way to represent 'competing evidence' without full probability. Scallop's top-k-proofs semiring is a direct model for 'the k best-established derivations'.

projects.name: LLM-proposer / symbolic-verifier systems for biomedical QA (KGARevion, AD-KG ASP verifier, MedRule-KG, OntoGPT/SPIRES, OntoURL)
projects.status: active research, nothing production: KGARevion ICLR 2025; AD-KG ICLR 2026 workshop poster; MedRule-KG preprint 2025-11; OntoGPT maintained (Monarch, PyPI 1.x 2025); OntoURL benchmark 2025
projects.what_it_does: KGARevion (Zitnik lab): LLM generates candidate triples, a KG-completion-fine-tuned LLM reviews them against a biomedical KG, revises, answers; +5-10% accuracy on medical QA; verification is embedding/KG-lookup, not logic. MedRule-KG: curated triples in prompt + deterministic rule checker after generation, -83% rule violations on 90 chemistry tasks. OntoGPT/SPIRES: LLM extraction into LinkML schemas grounded to OBO IDs - the practical tool for turning abstracts into ontology-term triples. OntoURL (57k questions, 40 ontologies): LLMs understand ontology terms but fail at ontological reasoning.
projects.relevance_to_biolean: Confirms the division of labour BioLean assumes - LLM proposes formal statements, a symbolic layer verifies - and shows where it breaks: autoformalization quality (F1 ~0.4 on biomedical text), not reasoning, is the bottleneck, and no system yet produces a checkable proof object or an evidence-weighted conclusion. BioLean's hand-annotated 'few hundred canonical publications' baseline sidesteps the extraction problem, and Lean certificates would be a real differentiator over KG-lookup verification. Use OntoGPT/SPIRES (plus the local PubTator3/BioREx relations) to draft candidate statements for human review, never as ground truth.

projects.name: Dead lineage: Prolog bio knowledge bases (Blipkit, Thea) and full OWL-DL reasoners (HermiT, Pellet)
projects.status: dead - Blipkit last commit 2016-08; Thea (OWL in Prolog) 2019-08; HermiT 2017-10 (last release 1.3.8, 2013); Pellet 2017-01; Openllet has 2025 commits but no release since 2019
projects.what_it_does: Blipkit was Mungall's SWI-Prolog deductive database over OBO/OWL ontologies, GO annotations and genomes (underpinning Obol); Thea loaded OWL into Prolog. HermiT and Pellet were the complete SROIQ (OWL 2 DL) tableau/hypertableau reasoners used in the 2008-2015 OBO era.
projects.relevance_to_biolean: Two lessons from what died. (1) The Prolog KB approach lost to 'data in standard formats + small replaceable reasoners': Mungall himself moved from Blipkit to OWL/ELK, then Whelk/relation-graph/Ubergraph. BioLean's statements should be a documented data format (TSV/LinkML/JSON) first and a Lean library second, or the library dies with its author. (2) Nobody in biology runs full OWL 2 DL any more; every live tool is EL(+RL) or Datalog. Staying inside EL/Horn expressivity is what keeps reasoning PTIME and Lean checking tractable; if a BioLean claim needs disjunction or negation, that is a signal to push it to the ASP layer, not to a DL reasoner.

key_lessons: The 'Datalog finds, Lean checks' loop is already built and verified: Nemo `--trace` -> JSON proof DAG -> CertifyingDatalog (Lean 4, ITP 2025) certifies 1000 GALEN-ontology conclusions in ~0.3 s. Reuse it; the gap to fill is that it certifies positive Datalog only and carries no weights.

Treat OBO as a precomputed fact base, not something to reason over: Ubergraph's nonredundant edge tables (46k part_of, 2.9k regulates class edges...) load straight into DuckDB/Nemo. RO's 102 property-chain axioms (e.g. enables o causally_upstream_of -> acts_upstream_of) are Horn rules and are the natural first lemmas of biolib.

GO-CAM already has the statement shape Dan describes - (activity, RO relation, activity, ECO code, PMID) as OWL individuals - with thousands of curated models in Turtle. Adopt that shape and ECO as the evidence-type axis rather than inventing a schema; what GO-CAM lacks (aggregated confidence, derived higher-level claims, proof objects) is exactly BioLean's contribution.

Evidence weighting has a canonical formalism: semiring provenance (Green et al. 2007; Scallop; Bourgaux KR 2022 for recursion). The weight of a derived claim is a semiring value over its certified proof tree - product/min along a chain, sum/max over independent supports - so Lean can check structure and score together. ProbLog's Biomine experience warns that independent-probability semantics overcount correlated literature (one experiment, fifty citing papers).

Competing hypotheses are what ASP is for: caspo's 11,700 data-compatible models and iggy's minimal inconsistent cores show stable models as 'worlds the evidence allows' and repairs as 'what must be wrong'. But non-monotonic conclusions have no proof trees, so keep ASP (clingo/plingo) as a hypothesis-enumeration layer and certify only the monotone derivations in Lean.

The 2025-26 neuro-symbolic systems (KGARevion, AD-KG ASP verifier, MedRule-KG) all converge on LLM-proposes / symbolic-verifies, and all show autoformalization (entity F1 ~0.41 on Alzheimer's text) rather than reasoning as the bottleneck. A hand-annotated canonical baseline plus Lean certificates is a genuine differentiator; use OntoGPT/SPIRES and local PubTator3 relations only to draft candidates.

Biology abandoned full OWL 2 DL (HermiT/Pellet dead since 2017) for EL(+RL) and Datalog (ELK -> Whelk -> relation-graph -> Nemo). Stay inside Horn/EL expressivity: it is what keeps reasoning polynomial and Lean checking cheap; disjunction or negation is the cue to route a statement to the ASP layer.

Prolog-era bio knowledge bases (Blipkit, Thea) died with their authors while their data survived in standard formats. Make BioLean's statements a documented data format (TSV/LinkML/JSON with PMIDs and ECO) first and a Lean library second.

Lean 4 formalisations of EL++/SROIQ now exist from a bio-ontology group (Baobab, Moose, 2026) and VEL found an error in the textbook EL completeness proof - evidence both that OBO semantics can be stated in Lean and that it should be, but Baobab is a two-month-old paper artifact, so audit before depending on it.
open_questions: Which semiring? Literature evidence is correlated (replications, reviews citing one experiment); independent-probability (ProbLog) overcounts and max-only (Viterbi) ignores replication. BioLean needs a dedup/independence model (per experiment? per lab? per ECO class?) before any score is meaningful - nobody in this angle has one.

Can a non-monotonic ASP conclusion get a Lean-checkable certificate? Checking that a given interpretation is a stable model is polynomial for normal programs, but 'X holds in every answer set' (cautious consequence) needs re-solving; is 'certified under this explicit world' acceptable for biolib claims?

CertifyingDatalog covers positive Datalog; Nemo's stratified negation, existential rules and aggregates are not certified. How much of RO/GO reasoning and of 'drug reduces hunger' style claims needs negation ('not degraded', 'absent in knockout')?
The Nemo->CertifyingDatalog conversion scripts target Nemo 0.7.1 trace output; Nemo is at 0.10.1. Does the trace format still convert, and will the Dresden group accept a BioLean use case?

RO has 704 relations with many near-synonyms; GO-CAM restricts to ~20. Which fixed subset should BioLean statements use, and how are ontology axioms (weight 1, definitional) kept distinct from empirical edges (weighted) in the same proof tree?

Does Ubergraph's build (41 ontologies, class-level) give enough instance-level material, or must BioLean materialise its own closure over UniProt/CHEBI individuals with relation-graph (--output-individuals) or Nemo EL rules?
Are Baobab's Lean sources (1.9 MB, June 2026) a usable library for OWL EL semantics in Lean, or paper-only code with no API stability? Nobody has reviewed them yet.

angle: Reasoning under uncertainty and with conflicting evidence: formal frameworks (subjective logic, Dempster-Shafer, probabilistic logic programming, MLN/PSL, Bayesian/causal DAGs, argumentation and defeasible logic, clinical evidence grading, INDRA-style belief) — assessed as candidates for what sits under a Lean proof system whose axioms are weighted literature statements.

projects.name: INDRA Belief Engine (indra.belief)
projects.status: active — PyPI indra 1.24.0 (2025-07-30), repo pushed 2026-06-30, BSD-2-Clause. Installed locally at ~/.cache/uv/.../indra 1.24.0.
projects.what_it_does: Assigns each Statement a probability that it is a *correct extraction*. SimpleScorer: for each source s, error term = e_syst[s] + prod(e_rand of each evidence from s); belief = 1 − product over sources. So many mentions from one reader saturate at 1−e_syst, while a second independent source multiplies. Negative evidence: score = p_pos × (1 − p_neg). Hierarchy: evidence from more-specific (refining) statements flows up to general ones, never down. Linked (inferred) statements get the product of their sources' beliefs. BayesianScorer re-estimates e_rand from curation counts (e_syst fixed 0.05). The 2023 MSB paper trained a Random Forest on 1,689 curated statements (features: per-reader mention counts, curated-DB overlap, sentence features); AUPRC 0.942, calibrated vs BioGRID membership. Actual default table on disk: e_rand reach/sparser/medscan/trips/rlimsp = 0.3, biopax 0.2, signor/ndex 0.049, phosphosite/biogrid 0.01; e_syst readers 0.05, curated DBs 0.01, gnbr 0.1.
projects.relevance_to_biolean: Directly reusable number type and code: the sibling project already exports INDRA Statement JSON, so every candidate axiom can arrive with a belief score and its evidence list. The independence-across-sources/saturation-within-source product is the simplest defensible fusion rule and is a one-line Lean definition. Two warnings: (1) INDRA belief is P(reader read the sentence right), not P(the biology is true) — BioLean needs a second layer for 'how established'; (2) the 2023 paper explicitly lists 'dealing with contradictions between Statements' and 'causal transitivity across multiple Statements' as unsolved — exactly BioLean's two hard problems.

projects.name: ACMG/AMP Bayesian framework + ClinGen gene-disease validity scoring (Tavtigian; Strande; SOP v12)
projects.status: active — ClinGen Gene-Disease Validity SOP Version 12 dated 2026-02-02; LR/points system being adopted into the ACMG/AMP v4 revision; R package acmgscaler on CRAN.
projects.what_it_does: Tavtigian 2018 turned the qualitative ACMG/AMP variant rules into a naive Bayes classifier: prior P(path)=0.10, each evidence category is a likelihood ratio (OddsPath) on an exponential scale, very strong 350 : strong 350^(1/2) : moderate 350^(1/4) : supporting 350^(1/8) ≈ 2.08; pathogenic and benign evidence multiply as odds; posterior thresholds Pathogenic >0.99, LP 0.90–0.99, VUS 0.10–0.90, LB/B below. Found 2 of 18 existing combining rules were inconsistent. Tavtigian 2020 re-expressed this as additive integer points = log_2.08(odds) (1/2/4/8). ClinGen gene-disease validity (Strande 2017, SOP v12): curators score genetic evidence (case-level variants, segregation, case-control; cap 12) and experimental evidence (function, functional alteration, models/rescue; cap 6), sum to 18; Limited 0.1–6, Moderate 7–11, Strong 12–18, Definitive = 12–18 AND replicated in independent publications over >3 years. Contradictory evidence yields Disputed/Refuted by expert panel judgement, not arithmetic.
projects.relevance_to_biolean: This is the only evidence-weighting scheme where a biology community already agreed on the numbers and the combination rule, and it is literally additive log-odds with per-category caps and a replication-over-time bonus — trivially encodable in Lean (Int points, min for caps, threshold functions) and auditable by biologists. Copy its shape for BioLean axioms: evidence-type → points, cap per type, sum → class, 'Definitive' requires independent replication. Also note what it does NOT formalise: conflict resolution is a human verdict ('Disputed'), which tells you where the formal system must hand off to argumentation.

projects.name: Subjective Logic (Jøsang) — opinions, cumulative/averaging fusion, deduction
projects.status: theory mature (book 2016); implementations toy-grade: subjective-logic 1.0.2 on PyPI (2025-07-27, 2 GitHub stars, MIT), doxa (first push 2026-10-19, 1 star). No widely used library exists.
projects.what_it_does: An opinion on a proposition is (belief b, disbelief d, uncertainty u, base rate a) with b+d+u=1; it is equivalent to a Beta(r+2a, s+2(1−a)) distribution, i.e. positive/negative evidence counts. Cumulative fusion (independent evidence) just adds pseudo-counts and shrinks u; averaging fusion (same evidence, different interpreters) averages; belief-constraint fusion is Dempster-like. Deduction/abduction propagate opinions along conditionals; trust discounting scales an opinion by trust in its source. Contradiction is visible: two confident opposite opinions fuse to high b AND high d with low u (a 'dogmatic conflict'), distinct from 'no evidence' (u≈1); probability collapses both to 0.5. Caveats: several multi-source operators are not associative, and van der Heijden et al. 2018 published corrections to the fusion operators — implement from the corrected forms.
projects.relevance_to_biolean: Best candidate for the *edge-weight type* if Dan wants 'nothing known' ≠ 'contested'. It is a record with one linear constraint plus rational-function operators, so a Lean structure with proofs of closure, commutativity and the (limited) associativity is realistic and small; and since cumulative fusion = adding (r,s) counts it stays interpretable as 'number of independent supporting/refuting papers'. You would write the ~300 lines yourself rather than depend on the 2-star packages. The 2025 'Subjective Logic Encodings' paper (Vasilakes, Zerva, Ananiadou) uses the same algebra to encode annotator disagreement — relevant to BioLean's manual annotation stage.

projects.name: Dempster-Shafer theory / belief functions (evidencelib, pyds, Bel-Games Coq)
projects.status: theory mature (1967/1976); evidencelib 1.3.0 on PyPI 2026-10-09 (MIT, active); pyds archived 2021 (maintainer recommends probabilistic alternatives); R dst on CRAN; Bel-Games Coq library last push 2023-11 (dormant). No Lean or Isabelle formalisation found.
projects.what_it_does: Mass functions on the power set of a frame; belief = mass of subsets, plausibility = 1 − belief of complement. Dempster's rule combines independent sources by conjunction and renormalises away conflict mass — this is where it breaks under contradiction (Zadeh's paradox: two nearly-opposite confident sources yield a certain conclusion neither supports). Hence the zoo of alternatives (Yager, Dubois-Prade, PCR5/6, DSmT), all implemented in evidencelib. Bel-Games (ITP 2023) is the one mechanised development: belief functions with finite support in Coq/SSReflect, used for game theory, not combination rules. Dezert et al. 2018 showed Shafer's own conditioning proof in the 1976 book is wrong — an argument for mechanisation.
projects.relevance_to_biolean: For binary propositions ('X inhibits Y': yes/no) DS collapses to a subjective-logic opinion, so there is no gain over SL and you inherit the conflict-renormalisation problem. Where DS genuinely adds something is multi-hypothesis frames (which of 5 mechanisms?), but the 2^n blow-up and the unsettled choice of combination rule make it a poor foundation. Encoding in Lean is natural (Finset powerset, Finset.sum) but exponential frames stay symbolic only. Take: use DS vocabulary (belief vs plausibility bounds) as a way to *report* an interval, not as the core calculus.
projects.reusable_assets: evidencelib (Python; Dempster, conjunctive, disjunctive, Yager, Dubois-Prade, PCR1-6, discounting, DSmT); Bel-Games Coq sources (MIT) as a template for finite-support belief functions.

projects.name: ProbLog / DeepProbLog (KU Leuven) + verified weighted model counting in Lean 4 (CPOG)
projects.status: ProbLog active (PyPI 2.3.0 2026-09-09, repo commits 2026-09-14, Apache-2.0); DeepProbLog active (PyPI 2.1.0 2026-09-07, repo 2026-09-29); CPOG Lean checker last push 2025-02 (research artefact, MIT). PRISM (Sato/Kameya) is effectively dead — no release traceable after 2.x.
projects.what_it_does: ProbLog = Prolog with independent probabilistic facts (distribution semantics). The probability of a query is the weighted model count of its proofs, computed by knowledge compilation (SDD / d-DNNF). Multiple derivations of the same fact combine automatically as noisy-OR, i.e. the same independent-evidence product INDRA uses. Conditioning via evidence/1; contradiction is not expressible — a fact and its negation with both probabilities cannot coexist, inconsistent evidence raises an error, and negation is stratified. DeepProbLog adds neural predicates. Separately, Bryant, Nawrocki, Avigad, Heule built in Lean 4 'the first formally verified toolchain for weighted and unweighted model counting': the D4 compiler emits a CPOG certificate, a Lean-verified checker validates it and evaluates the weighted count.
projects.relevance_to_biolean: ProbLog is the cleanest executable semantics for 'statements are weighted axioms, derive a weighted conclusion', and the Ozempic chain is a 3-line ProbLog program. But it cannot represent 'paper A says inhibits, paper B says no effect'. The deeper lesson is architectural: do not run probabilistic inference inside Lean; compute outside (ProbLog/D4) and have Lean check a certificate. CPOG is a proof-of-concept that this pattern already exists in Lean 4 for exactly the computation ProbLog performs. A BioLean 'proof carrying an evidence score' could be a Lean term + certified WMC.
projects.reusable_assets: problog Python package (SDD/d-DNNF inference, learning from interpretations), DeepProbLog, CPOG tooling and Lean 4 checker (rebryant/cpog).

projects.name: Scallop (provenance-semiring Datalog)
projects.status: active — repo pushed 2026-06-26, 520 stars, MIT, Rust + scallopy Python binding (build with maturin; the PyPI scallopy 0.1.0 from 2021 is stale).
projects.what_it_does: Datalog with recursion, aggregation, stratified negation, where every tuple carries a tag from a provenance semiring. Swapping the semiring changes the reasoning mode with the same program: unit (boolean), minmaxprob (weakest-link/strongest-path probability), top-k proofs (keeps the k best derivations as explanations), differentiable variants for training with PyTorch. Conjunction along a derivation = ⊗, alternative derivations = ⊕. No contradiction handling beyond stratified negation.
projects.relevance_to_biolean: The semiring abstraction is the right 'shape' for a biolib score: a proof term's evidence score is ⊗ along the derivation and ⊕ across alternative proofs, and you can defer the choice of algebra (log-odds sum, min, SL opinion) to a type-class parameter. Mathlib already has Semiring and ordered semirings, so a semiring-valued derivation relation is a natural Lean definition; top-k-proofs provenance is exactly 'show me the best-supported chain of papers for this claim'. Scallop itself is a research compiler, not infrastructure — take the idea, not the dependency.
