projects.name: Markov Logic Networks and Probabilistic Soft Logic (PSL)
projects.status: MLN tooling dead: Alchemy and Tuffy unmaintained for >10 years, pracmln last release 2019-05. PSL maintained: pslpython 2.4.1 released 2026-10-06, Java core repo pushed 2024-06, Apache-2.0.
projects.what_it_does: MLN: weighted first-order clauses define a Markov random field over groundings; inference is #P-hard, approximated by MCMC/MaxWalkSAT. PSL: same idea with Łukasiewicz t-norm relaxation to [0,1] truth values, making MAP inference a convex optimisation (hinge-loss MRF) that scales; weights are learned. Conflicting rules do not break anything — they trade off through weights, so contradiction is handled 'gracefully' by soft truth values. Applied to drug-target interaction (Fakhraei 2014; meta-path PSL 2023) and drug-drug interaction prediction.
projects.relevance_to_biolean: Fails as a foundation for BioLean: inference is a global optimisation with no proof objects, so there is nothing to reuse as a lemma and no derivation to show a biologist; adding one axiom can move every truth value. PSL's Łukasiewicz semantics is formalisable (a small 2025 Lean project by Macovei encodes MV-algebras, 0 stars, not Mathlib) but the value of PSL is the solver, which is anti-proof. Possibly useful as an external oracle to *propose* weights or detect inconsistent axiom sets, not as the logic.

projects.name: Argumentation frameworks and defeasible logic (Dung AF, ASPIC+, ABA, DeLP, Carneades; epistemic probabilistic AFs; Isabelle/HOL formalisation)
projects.status: TweetyProject 1.31 released 2026-07-14 (Java, LGPL-3, active, repo pushed 2026-10-18). PyArg last push 2024-09 (dormant, MIT); pygarg 2024 (abstract AFs only); Carneades-4 last commit 2024-10 (dormant); SPINdle dormant. Isabelle/HOL formalisation of Dung semantics (Steen & Fuenmayor 2021) repo last push 2021-10. No Lean/Coq/Agda formalisation of argumentation found. ICCMA 2025 ran an ABA track.
projects.what_it_does: Dung AF: arguments + attack relation; semantics (grounded, complete, preferred, stable, ...) pick acceptable sets. Grounded extension is the least fixed point of the defence operator — unique and polynomial. ASPIC+ builds arguments from strict and defeasible rules with preferences, giving rebut/undercut/undermine attacks; ABA and DeLP are related structured systems. Hunter & Thimm's epistemic approach attaches probabilities to arguments under rationality constraints (if P(A)>0.5 and A attacks B then P(B)≤0.5), subsuming Dung; epistemic graphs (2020) generalise to degrees of belief/disbelief. Hunter & Williams 2012 applied this to clinical trials: arguments for 'treatment X superior' from evidence tables, with meta-arguments that attack arguments based on weaker evidence. Steen & Fuenmayor encoded all standard semantics in Isabelle/HOL, verified Dung's fundamental lemma, showed a naive labelling lemma false by counter-model, and used Nitpick to compute extensions. Tweety implements all of this (arg.dung, arg.prob, arg.aspic, arg.aba, arg.delp, arg.weighted, arg.rankings, logics.pcl).
projects.relevance_to_biolean: This is the only family that treats contradiction as first-class: competing hypotheses are arguments, 'inhibits' vs 'no effect' is an attack, and 'better established' is a preference that decides which attack succeeds — exactly Dan's open problem, and exactly what ClinGen does by hand with 'Disputed'. Lean encoding is natural and small: an AF is a type with a relation; grounded semantics via Mathlib's Knaster–Tarski (OrderHom.lfp); porting Steen & Fuenmayor is a well-scoped first Lean project and a good smoke test. ASPIC+ maps onto BioLean directly: strict rules = ontology axioms (RO, GO is_a), defeasible rules = literature statements, preferences = evidence scores. Weakness: combining argumentation with numeric weights (ranking semantics, epistemic probabilities) is an active research area with no consensus, and non-monotonicity means a BioLean theorem must be indexed by the corpus version.

projects.name: Evidence-grading schemes as inference rules: GRADE, Oxford CEBM levels, GO evidence codes / ECO
projects.status: GRADE active (GRADE Ontology v1 of 89 terms 2024–2025; GRADErater official automation tool announced 2026); Oxford CEBM levels static since 2011; ECO active (OBO Foundry; Dan has it locally); GO evidence-code reliability literature 2008–2016.
projects.what_it_does: GRADE rates a body of evidence High/Moderate/Low/Very low by starting from study design and applying up/down-grades for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision, publication bias — a judgement protocol, not a calculus. Automation attempts: URSE-automated reached 63% agreement with humans (κ 0.44) on 115 Cochrane reviews; GRADE's own group concludes full automation is 'not opportune'; GRADErater codifies explicit decision rules. Oxford CEBM is a static study-design hierarchy. In molecular biology the native scheme is GO evidence codes mapped to ECO classes (IDA, IMP, IPI, TAS, IEA, ...). Škunca et al. 2012 measured electronic (IEA) annotation reliability from GOA release-to-release changes and found it rivals non-experimental curated codes; the GO 'Pitfalls' review notes IDA is most direct, IMP/IGI derivative, IPI guilt-by-association for process terms, and that codes 'cannot be used directly to exclude low-confidence data'.
projects.relevance_to_biolean: GRADE/CEBM teach what not to do: don't try to mechanise judgement-heavy grading — use them only as labels on axioms. ECO is the asset: BioLean already has 1.28M GOA annotation→PMID links each carrying an ECO code, so the cheapest workable weighting is an ECO-class → log-odds-points table in the ACMG style (IDA 4, IMP/IGI 2, IPI 1–2 by aspect, TAS 1, IEA calibrated from Škunca-style reliability). That gives one scalar per edge today, from data on disk, with a clear upgrade path to subjective-logic opinions later.

projects.name: OpenCog PLN (Probabilistic Logic Networks) + Bio-AtomSpace
projects.status: dormant — opencog/pln last push 2025-09 (16 stars); classic OpenCog superseded by Hyperon/MeTTa (trueagi-io, active 2026-02) where PLN is being re-implemented. Bio-AtomSpace papers 2015–2020.
projects.what_it_does: Uncertain term logic with truth values (strength s, confidence c), c = n/(n+k) from evidence count n and a 'personality parameter' k; indefinite (interval) truth values; inference rules (deduction, induction, abduction, revision) propagate them through a hypergraph. Bio-AtomSpace loaded GO, pathways and expression data and ran PLN to produce 'uncertain logical explanations' linking genes to GO categories and longevity. The 2020 paper describes results as preliminary and inference control as the open issue; a 2024 Goertzel paper compares PLN with NARS and finds similar s×c outputs under high uncertainty.
projects.relevance_to_biolean: The closest historical precedent to the BioLean vision — formalise biology over GO with uncertain truth values and derive higher-level claims — and it produced no reusable library after ~15 years. The failure modes are instructive: forward-chaining explosion with no inference control, truth values not tied to citable statements, and no proof objects for reuse. BioLean's distinguishing design decisions should be the opposite on all three: goal-directed proofs, every axiom is a referenced sentence, and reuse via proved lemmas (mathlib-style) rather than a growing hypergraph.

key_lessons: Separate 'probability the extraction is right' from 'probability the biology is true'. INDRA's belief (and its 0.942-AUPRC Random Forest) models only the first; the 2023 MSB paper lists contradictions and causal transitivity as unsolved. BioLean needs the second layer explicitly.

Every working fusion rule is the same move — assume independence across sources, saturate within a source: INDRA's 1 − Π(e_syst + Π e_rand), ProbLog's noisy-OR over derivations, subjective-logic cumulative fusion (add Beta pseudo-counts), ACMG's sum of log-odds points. Pick one, state the independence assumption as a hypothesis, make it a Lean lemma.

The ACMG/ClinGen point system (Tavtigian 2018/2020, SOP v12 2026) is the only weighting scheme biologists already agreed numbers for, and it is additive integer log-odds with per-category caps and a replication-over-time bonus. Copy its shape; it is trivially formalisable and auditable.

Probability does not resolve contradiction: Dempster's rule renormalises it away (Zadeh paradox), ProbLog cannot express it, Bayesian nets just lower posteriors, PSL smears it into soft values. The frameworks that treat it as first-class are argumentation (ASPIC+, Hunter & Williams 2012 meta-arguments attacking weaker evidence) and ClinGen's human 'Disputed/Refuted'. A BioLean theorem should carry its set of undefeated attackers, not only a number.

Provenance semirings (Scallop; Green et al. 2007) are the right abstraction for a biolib score: ⊗ along a derivation, ⊕ across alternative derivations, with the algebra as a type-class parameter so log-odds, min (weakest link) and SL opinions are interchangeable. Mathlib already has semirings.

Compute outside, certify inside. The Lean 4 verified weighted-model-counting checker (Bryant, Nawrocki, Avigad, Heule 2025) does for D4/ProbLog-style inference exactly what BioLean should do for evidence arithmetic: external tool produces a certificate, Lean checks it. Do not try to run probabilistic inference in the kernel.

Mechanising this area is cheap and finds real errors: Steen & Fuenmayor's Isabelle encoding exposed a false labelling lemma; Dezert et al. showed Shafer's 1976 conditioning proof wrong. A Lean port of Dung AFs with grounded semantics via Mathlib's lfp is a small first project and a good smoke test for the whole programme.

Subjective-logic opinions (b,d,u) are the best edge-weight type if 'no evidence' must differ from 'conflicting evidence'; probability collapses both to 0.5. Libraries are toy-grade (2 stars), so write the ~300 lines yourself from the corrected operators (van der Heijden et al. 2018) and keep the Beta pseudo-count reading so biologists can interpret it.

Reject global joint inference (MLN/PSL) as the core: no proof objects, non-compositional (one new axiom moves every value), and MLN tooling is dead. At most use PSL as an external oracle for proposing weights or flagging inconsistent axiom sets.

OpenCog PLN/Bio-AtomSpace already tried 'uncertain logic over GO' for a decade and left nothing reusable; failures were forward-chaining explosion, truth values not tied to citations, and no reusable lemmas. BioLean's design should invert all three.

Judgement-heavy grading does not mechanise (URSE-automated 63% agreement, GRADE group says full automation 'not opportune'). Use GRADE/CEBM as labels, and use ECO — already on disk with 1.28M GOA→PMID links — as the evidence-type vocabulary, mapped to ACMG-style points (Škunca 2012 gives IEA reliability estimates).
open_questions: Which algebra for edge weights: scalar log-odds (ACMG-style), subjective-logic opinion (b,d,u), or DS mass? This decides whether 'unknown' and 'contested' are distinguishable and whether weights add or fuse.

Literature evidence is heavily non-independent (same lab, same assay, citation cascades, review-of-review). INDRA fudges this with per-source saturation; SL offers averaging vs cumulative fusion. Can dependence be estimated from PMIDs, author overlap, MeSH, or the Open Targets/PubTator co-mention data already on disk?

How does evidence compose along a chain (the Ozempic example)? Product of beliefs (INDRA linked statements) is only valid under independence; min (Scallop minmaxprob) is a weakest-link heuristic. Should Lean prove interval bounds rather than point values?

Argumentation is non-monotonic (a new paper can defeat a proof) but Lean is monotonic. Does a BioLean theorem become 'P, relative to corpus snapshot v' with the attacker set as an explicit hypothesis, and how is that kept honest as the corpus grows?

Most apparent contradictions are context differences (species, tissue, dose, timescale). Does context live in the statement (more ontology terms), in the weight, or in the attack relation (ASPIC+ undercutters)?

What exactly is proved when weights come from a trained model (INDRA RF) or a curator's judgement: only the arithmetic given the axiom weights, or also the derivation of the weights? Where is the trusted base?

Can ECO classes be calibrated to likelihood ratios the way ClinGen calibrated functional assays (PS3/BS3)? Škunca gives reliability for IEA; nothing comparable exists for TAS, IMP, or text-mined relations.

Is porting Steen & Fuenmayor's Isabelle argumentation formalisation to Lean 4 (grounded semantics via Mathlib lfp) worth doing first as the proof-system skeleton, or should the skeleton be a semiring-valued derivation relation with argumentation added as the defeat layer?

angle: Formal methods and proof assistants applied to biology (Lean/Rocq/Isabelle/HOL/Maude, rule-based modelling, formal ontology, autoformalization of science, and how Lean/Mathlib practice maps onto an evidence-carrying "biolib")

key_lessons: Literature statements as named Lean axioms is the canonical encoding: `#print axioms` on any proved claim then lists exactly the PMID-tagged axioms it rests on (verified on Lean 4.35.0 in /tmp/biolean_probe). crnt-lean shows the CI pattern: an AxiomAudit.lean that pins #print axioms on headline results and fails the build on sorryAx or unexpected axioms.

Lean's Prop is proof-irrelevant (two proofs of the same statement are `rfl`-equal), so evidence scores cannot live on proofs. Either compute scores outside the kernel over the axiom dependency graph (gonzalgo-style), or make claims data: semiring-annotated facts as in provenance-lean, or a `Supported p` record (score, refs, proof), with Lean proving the aggregation is sound/monotone, as the 2026 patent-analysis Lean pipeline does with a verified lattice.

Use provenance semirings (Green et al. 2007; provenance-lean, Lean 4, MIT, active Oct 2026) as the evidence algebra: polynomial semiring gives the exact PMID-support formula for a derived claim, Viterbi gives best-derivation belief, Boolean gives plain truth. One proof structure, several scorings, and INDRA's belief engine becomes a special case rather than a bespoke rule.

Physlib's `informal_definition` / `informal_lemma` (docstring + references + `deps` + `tag`) and 'semiformal' (type stated, proof wanted) declarations are the right onboarding ladder for a corpus: most of biolib will be informal statements for years, and Physlib already has the metaprogramming to make them first-class and to draw informal-vs-formal dependency graphs.

Prove relational and structural claims, not dynamics. HyLL (2014), Zsyntax in HOL (2017) and the Rocq neuronal archetypes (2025) all stayed at 'relatively simple examples' because they proved temporal behaviour of models by hand. The Ozempic-style chain (inhibits, has_function, breakdown_of) is relational and Datalog/EL-shaped; leave kinetics to BIOCHAM/Kappa/BioNetGen.

Zsyntax (Boniolo et al. 2010; HOL formalisation Rashid et al. 2017) is the direct ancestor of 'pathway = proof from literature reactions' and was designed for text mining; its three connectives are a starting calculus. It died from manual-proof cost and lack of community, both of which Lean + Mathlib practice addresses.

Pathway Logic proves a literature-curated formal rule base of hundreds of referenced rules is feasible, and that it dies if it is single-lab and tied to a niche engine (site frozen since 2017 although Maude is alive in 2026). Its typed state (entity + location + modification) is richer than a bare ontology triple and is what a BioLean statement schema should carry.

BIOCHAM shows 'experimental knowledge as formulae, validation as checking' works in practice, and its QFLTL satisfaction degree is an existing graded-truth precedent. Konur et al.'s 2023 'Verifiable biology' review found 30+ model checkers and no theorem provers in use, all driven by computer scientists: biologist-facing usability, not logic, is the blocker.

Autoformalization of science is affordable but drifts: FormalScience (ACL 2026) got 200 Lean-formalised physics problems for ~50 USD with one expert, yet its main result is a taxonomy of semantic drift (notational collapse, abstraction elevation) where Lean accepts a statement that lost the science. BioLean's ontology-term annotation step needs a fidelity check independent of the type checker.

Do not elaborate 6M OBO terms as Lean axioms. GO/CHEBI/MONDO/RO are OWL 2 EL; VEL (Coq, 2024) shows a verified EL++ classifier is feasible and, tellingly, found two errors in the published algorithm's completeness proof. Compute the hierarchy externally and import certificates or a trimmed closure.

Treat `native_decide` as a lower trust tier: it adds a per-theorem axiom that trusts the compiler (verified locally; gonzalgo `trust` flags it). `decide`, `simp`, `omega` and Aesop (active, Oct 2026) stay kernel-checked and are the automation to lean on for RO-chain reasoning.

Josephson's two habits transfer directly: every scientific premise is an explicit named hypothesis in the theorem statement, and definitions are typeclass-polymorphic so the same biolib definition is proved over R and executed over Float. INDRA -> PySB -> BioNetGen/Kappa already exists for simulation, so BioLean should sit beside it as the proof layer consuming the same INDRA Statement JSON.
open_questions: Competing hypotheses: no formal-methods-in-biology project represents them. Closest is Risk Agoras (dialectical argumentation for carcinogenicity, ~2000) and weighted bipolar argumentation frameworks (2025, non-bio). Is it enough to encode rival claims as two axioms with scores and detect conflict via the axiom graph, or does BioLean need a paraconsistent/argumentation layer?

Where does the evidence algebra live: inside Lean (provenance-lean semiring annotations, proofs about aggregation) or outside (gonzalgo-style walk over #print axioms)? Proof irrelevance forces a choice early and it shapes the whole schema.

Which fragment is decidable enough for `decide`/Aesop? RO chains over is_a/part_of/regulates look EL/Datalog-shaped, but 'is responsible for breakdown of hormone' mixes GO function, process and CHEBI roles; needs a worked example before committing a schema.

How to check fidelity of autoformalised triples (FormalScience's semantic drift) when the target is ontology IDs rather than equations: back-translation, ECO codes, PubTator3/BioREx agreement, or human curation of the few hundred canonical papers?
Ontology import strategy: trimmed Lean axioms for the terms actually used vs a verified external EL reasoner (VEL pattern) producing certificates; neither has been tried at OBO scale.
Whether Pathway Logic's curated signalling rules (if still downloadable) and INDRA Statements can be mechanically lifted into BioLean axioms, giving a non-trivial baseline before any new curation.

K-Lean is private/commercial and VeriBiota is a one-org tool; nothing reusable confirmed, but worth a one-line email to Kenosian only if their contracts turn out to overlap with planned biolib lemmas.
